planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last expected frost, since Capsicum chinense germinates slowly and needs a long warm season to ripen.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost using a heat mat to keep soil near 85F, since chinense types germinate unevenly and slowly compared to annuum peppers. Transplant into warm soil only after nighttime temperatures stay reliably above 60F, and stake plants as the heavy fruit load develops. Pepper X was bred by Ed Currie of PuckerButt Pepper Company and was certified by Guinness World Records in 2023 as the hottest pepper ever measured, surpassing the Carolina Reaper. Handle ripe pods with gloves, as the capsaicin level is extreme even by superhot standards.

common_name: Naga Morich Pepper (Snake Pepper, Bangladeshi Naga)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost on a heat mat, then transplant once soil has warmed thoroughly.

directions: Sow indoors 8-10 weeks ahead of the last frost, providing bottom heat to speed the naturally slow chinense germination, and pot up seedlings before setting them out in warm soil. Give plants a long, hot growing season and steady moisture for the heaviest pod set. Naga Morich is a traditional Bangladeshi and northeastern Indian pepper closely related to bhut jolokia, prized for its intense heat and slightly fruity aroma, and it is a parent of several later superhot hybrids. Pods ripen from green to a wrinkled orange-red and should be handled with gloves.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, since this chinense type needs a long, warm season to fully ripen.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost with bottom heat to improve germination, then transplant into well-drained, fertile soil once the weather is reliably warm. Feed lightly and keep moisture consistent, since chinense peppers are prone to blossom drop under heat stress or drought. Devil's Tongue produces distinctively wrinkled, tapering pods and is closely related to habanero types, with heat that reaches well into the habanero-to-superhot range along with a fruity flavor. It is grown in shades ranging from pale yellow to deep red depending on the strain.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost using bottom heat, as chinense superhots germinate slowly and need a long season.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost on a heat mat, since germination can be slow and irregular, then transplant into warm, well-drained soil after all frost danger passes. Stake plants and prune early flowers to build a stronger frame before letting the heavy fruit set develop. This is the original Trinidad Scorpion strain from which the later 'Butch T' selection was bred, named for the narrow curled tail at the pod's tip and known for ferocious, lingering heat. Wear gloves when harvesting and processing the ripe red pods.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost with bottom heat, giving this slow-maturing superhot a long head start.

directions: Sow indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost with bottom heat, since chinense seed can take several weeks to germinate, and pot up seedlings before moving them to the garden once nights are reliably warm. Support the branching stems as fruit accumulates, and reduce watering slightly as pods mature to concentrate flavor. Douglah is a Trinidad 7 Pot strain that ripens to a distinctive dull brown 'chocolate' color rather than red, and it is regarded as one of the hottest of the 7 Pot varieties with a smoky, earthy flavor. Always wear gloves when handling ripe fruit.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

common_name: 7 Pot Brain Strain Pepper (Yellow Brain Strain)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost with bottom heat, as this superhot needs a long warm season to size up and ripen.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, keeping the medium warm to encourage the slow-to-sprout chinense seed, then transplant once the soil has warmed well past frost danger. Stake heavily loaded plants and keep watering even to prevent blossom end rot on the convoluted pods. Brain Strain is a 7 Pot type selected for its intensely wrinkled, brain-like fruit surface and sits among the hottest strains within the already fierce 7 Pot family. It is grown in both yellow and red-fruited forms, both intensely pungent.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost on a heat mat, since this hybrid superhot germinates slowly.

directions: Sow indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost with consistent bottom heat, then harden off and transplant once nights stay warm, since this hybrid resents cool, wet soil. Keep the compact plants evenly watered and staked once fruit sets heavily along the branches. Naga Viper was bred in England by crossing Bhut Jolokia, Naga Morich, and Trinidad Scorpion lines, and it briefly held recognition as the world's hottest pepper around 2011 before later superhots surpassed it. The knobby pods ripen from green to red and carry a sharp, lingering heat.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost with bottom heat, since chinense superhots are slow to germinate and mature.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost on a heat mat, and transplant only once the soil is thoroughly warm, since seedlings stall in cool conditions. Stake plants as the fruit load builds and keep moisture consistent to avoid blossom drop during heat spikes. Komodo Dragon was bred in the United Kingdom by chile grower Salvatore Genovese and is known as one of the hottest peppers developed in Britain, with elongated, ridged red pods and a sharp, intense burn. It is popular among superhot collectors for its productivity in cooler UK-style greenhouse growing.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

common_name: Filius Blue Ornamental Pepper (Color-Changing Compact Chile)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, then transplant into containers or beds once frost danger has passed.

directions: Sow indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant seedlings into pots or beds once nights are warm, since this compact annuum is often grown as a patio or container ornamental. Keep it evenly watered and in full sun for the heaviest, most colorful fruit display. Filius Blue is bred for its dense, upright habit and small purple-flushed leaves, with round fruits that ripen through purple and cream shades before finishing bright red, making the plant look multicolored all at once. The pods carry real heat and are edible, though the plant is grown mainly for its ornamental fruit color.

common_name: Cumari do Pará Pepper (Brazilian Wild Hot Pepper)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 7-9 weeks before the last frost on gentle bottom heat, then transplant once the weather is reliably warm.

directions: Start seed indoors 7-9 weeks before the last frost with gentle bottom heat, since this small-fruited chinense type is slow to establish, and transplant once nights stay warm. The bushy plants benefit from routine picking, which encourages continuous flowering and fruit set through the season. Cumari do Pará comes from the Pará region of Brazil and produces tiny, round to oval berry-like fruits on long thin stems that belie an intense, sharp heat, and it is traditionally used fresh, pickled in vinegar, or as a garnish. Its diminutive size makes it a good candidate for container growing despite the plant's habanero-relative heat level.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University
